title: Future Perfect Continuous
tagline: how long by a future time: will have been + -ing
why: Use it to say how long something will have been going on when we reach a future time. It is perfect for anniversaries, careers, long trips and long waits.
know: the form will have been + verb-ing: I'll have been working
the time words for + a length of time and by + a date or time
understand: that we stand at a future point and look back at how long an action will have continued
the difference between how long (future perfect continuous) and how many (future perfect)
able: say how long you will have been living, working or studying somewhere by a future date
talk about long waits and long trips: We'll have been driving for ten hours.
mistakes: By June I will have been work here for ten years.
By June I will have been working here for ten years.
By next month I will be living here for a year.
By next month I will have been living here for a year.
By May I will have been knowing her for ten years.
By May I will have known her for ten years.
By the time she will retire, she will have been nursing for 40 years.
By the time she retires, she will have been nursing for 40 years.
By 5 pm I will have been writing three reports.
By 5 pm I will have written three reports.
use: How long an action will have continued up to a future time: By June, I'll have been working here for ten years.
How long, up to a future event: When she retires, she'll have been teaching for 35 years.
To explain a future result: He'll be tired when he arrives. He'll have been driving all day.
form: I will have been working. / They'll have been waiting.
She won't have been living here long.
How long will you have been studying by June?
Yes, I will. / No, I won't.
signals: for + a length of time (for ten years, for six hours), by + a date (by next June, by 2030), by the time + present simple, when, all day, how long
tip: How long? Use will have been + -ing: I'll have been writing for three hours. How many? Use the future perfect: I'll have written three reports. State verbs like know use the future perfect too.

pick.q: By next June, I ___ in Canada for ten years.
pick.why: By next June + for ten years (how long): will have been living.

pick.q: By the time the plane ___, we will have been flying for fourteen hours.
pick.why: After by the time, use the present simple: lands, not will land.

pick.q: By 6 pm, the kids ___ video games for five hours straight.
pick.why: By 6 pm + for five hours: will have been playing. After been, add -ing.

pick.q: By May, I ___ my neighbour for twenty years.
pick.why: Know is a state verb, so no -ing. Use the future perfect: will have known.

pick.q: By the end of today, I ___ four reports.
pick.why: Four reports is how many, not how long, so use the future perfect: will have written.

pick.q: By the time he retires, Mr. Singh ___ buses in Toronto for thirty years.
pick.why: Looking back from a future point + for thirty years: will have been driving.

pick.q: By September, we ___ English together for two years.
pick.why: By September + for two years (how long up to then): will have been studying.

pick.q: At 3 o'clock tomorrow, the road crew ___ for exactly eight hours.
pick.why: At a future time + for eight hours: will have been working. After been, add -ing.

type.q: By the time the snowplow comes, it ___ (snow) for two days.
type.why: How long up to a future moment: will have been snowing.

type.q: By the time we ___ (reach) Winnipeg, we will have been driving for nine hours.
type.why: After by the time, use the present simple: reach, not will reach.

type.q: By midnight, the volunteers ___ (cook) for twelve hours.
type.why: By midnight + for twelve hours: will have been cooking.

type.q: When the guests arrive at 7, Grandma ___ (bake) since early morning.
type.why: How long up to 7 pm: will have been baking.

type.q: By the end of the concert, the band ___ (play) for three hours without a break.
type.why: By the end + for three hours: will have been playing (will have played is also possible).

type.q: By the time the ambulance arrives, the man ___ (lie) on the ice for an hour.
type.why: How long up to a future moment: will have been lying. Lie becomes lying.

type.q: By 3 pm, the patients ___ (sit) in the waiting room for five hours.
type.why: By 3 pm + for five hours: will have been sitting.

type.q: Don't worry, she ___ (not / wait) long when you arrive.
type.why: Negative: won't have been waiting (won't have waited is also possible).

spot.q: By next year, I will have been teach here for a decade.
spot.why: After will have been, use -ing: will have been teaching.

spot.q: By Friday, we will have been renovating the kitchen since six weeks.
spot.why: Use for with a length of time: for six weeks. Since goes with a starting point.

spot.q: By the time Mom will get home, the soup will have been simmering for hours.
spot.why: After by the time, use the present simple: gets.

spot.q: By August, I will be living in Halifax for five years.
spot.why: How long up to a future time: will have been living.

spot.q: By tonight, I will have been reading three chapters.
spot.why: Three chapters is how many, so use the future perfect: will have read.

order.a: By June I will have been working here for ten years.
alt: I will have been working here for ten years by June.
order.why: By June + subject + will have been working + place + for ten years.

order.a: How long will you have been living in Canada?
order.why: Question: How long + will + you + have been living + place.

order.a: They will have been driving all day by then.
alt: By then they will have been driving all day.
order.why: Subject + will have been driving + all day + by then.

order.a: She won't have been waiting for very long.
order.why: Negative: won't have been waiting + for very long.

pick.q: By the end of this year, my father ___ taxis for twenty-five years.
pick.why: By the end of this year + for 25 years: will have been driving.

pick.q: By the time the rain ___, it will have been raining for three days.
pick.why: After by the time, use the present simple: stops.

pick.q: By next week, I ___ this cough for a month!
pick.why: Have (a cough) is a state here, so no -ing: will have had.

pick.q: By noon, the movers ___ forty boxes into the truck.
pick.why: Forty boxes is how many, so use the future perfect: will have carried.

pick.q: By 2030, my brother ___ as a firefighter for twenty years.
pick.why: By 2030 + for twenty years: will have been working.

pick.q: When we finally board, we ___ at the gate for four hours.
pick.why: How long up to a future moment: will have been waiting. After been, add -ing.

type.q: By 9 pm, the baby ___ (cry) for an hour if nobody picks her up.
type.why: By 9 pm + for an hour: will have been crying.

type.q: By the time I ___ (finish) this degree, I will have been studying for six years.
type.why: After by the time, use the present simple: finish.

type.q: By December, our neighbours ___ (renovate) their house for a whole year.
type.why: By December + for a whole year: will have been renovating.

type.q: By the time you land, it ___ (rain) in Vancouver for a week.
type.why: How long up to a future moment: will have been raining.

type.q: By 5 pm, the workers ___ (dig) the new basement for ten hours.
type.why: By 5 pm + for ten hours: will have been digging. Dig becomes digging.

type.q: By next Christmas, my uncle ___ (fix) cars in his garage for fifty years.
type.why: By next Christmas + for fifty years: will have been fixing (will have fixed is also possible).

type.q: When the soup is ready, it ___ (boil) for three hours.
type.why: How long up to a future moment: will have been boiling.

type.q: We ___ (not / live) here long when the baby arrives.
type.why: Negative: won't have been living (won't have lived is also possible).

spot.q: By June, I will has been working at the bank for a year.
spot.why: After will, always use have: will have been working.

spot.q: By the time the bus will come, we will have been standing in the cold for an hour.
spot.why: After by the time, use the present simple: comes.

spot.q: By the end of the day, she will have been answering 200 emails.
spot.why: 200 emails is how many, so use the future perfect: will have answered.

spot.q: By next October, I will have been knowing my best friend for thirty years.
spot.why: Know is a state verb, so no -ing: will have known.

order.a: By March we will have been living here for five years.
alt: We will have been living here for five years by March.
order.why: By March + subject + will have been living + here + for five years.

order.a: How long will you have been working there by then?
order.why: Question: How long + will + you + have been working + there + by then.

order.a: He will have been sleeping for twelve hours.
order.why: Subject + will have been sleeping + for twelve hours.

bank.q: By next summer, my wife ___ yoga for ten years.
bank.why: By next summer + for ten years: will have been teaching.

bank.q: By the time we ___ Quebec City, we will have been cycling for a week.
bank.why: After by the time, use the present simple: reach.

bank.q: By Friday, I ___ my new boss for exactly one month.
bank.why: Know is a state verb, so no -ing: will have known.

bank.q: By the end of the night, the band ___ twenty songs.
bank.why: Twenty songs is how many, so use the future perfect: will have played.

bank.q: By 2028, the bakery ___ bread on this street for a century.
bank.why: By 2028 + for a century: will have been making.

bank.q: When you call at noon, I ___ in the garden for four hours.
bank.why: How long up to noon: will have been working. After been, add -ing.

bank.q: ___ you have been living in Edmonton for a year by Christmas?
bank.why: Question: Will + subject + have been + -ing. The answer is Will.

bank.q: By midnight, the snow ___ for twenty hours without stopping.
bank.why: By midnight + for twenty hours: will have been falling.

bank.q: By the time the movie ends, we ___ (sit) in this theatre for three hours.
bank.why: How long up to a future moment: will have been sitting (or we'll have been sitting).

bank.q: By next April, Rosa ___ (volunteer) at the food bank for two years.
bank.why: By next April + for two years: will have been volunteering (will have volunteered is also possible).

bank.q: By the time the plumber ___ (arrive), the water will have been leaking for six hours.
bank.why: After by the time, use the present simple: arrives.

bank.q: By the end of the shift, the nurses ___ (stand) for twelve hours.
bank.why: By the end of the shift + for twelve hours: will have been standing.

bank.q: By 10 am, the bread dough ___ (rise) for two hours.
bank.why: By 10 am + for two hours: will have been rising.

bank.q: By the time the race ends, the runners will have been running for over four hours.
bank.why: This sentence is correct: by the time + present simple (ends), then will have been running for + time.

bank.q: By next week, he will have been training since three months.
bank.why: Use for with a length of time: for three months.

bank.q: By next month, my parents will be running their shop for twenty years.
bank.why: How long up to a future time: will have been running their shop for twenty years.

bank.q: When the guests arrive, I will have been cooking all afternoon.
bank.why: This sentence is correct: will have been cooking shows how long up to a future moment.

bank.a: By then we will have been waiting for two hours.
alt: We will have been waiting for two hours by then.
bank.why: By then + subject + will have been waiting + for two hours.

bank.a: How long will she have been teaching by June?
bank.why: Question: How long + will + she + have been teaching + by June.

bank.a: The engine will have been running all night.
bank.why: Subject + will have been running + all night.
